author: Kaia Fleetarrow, of the Pine Hold lodges

#The Seasons of the Hunt

A good hunter knows not only how to shoot but when and where. This almanac collects what my family has learned in four generations of living from the forest.

#Elk and Deer

Elk graze the open meadows at dawn and dusk. They are wary but curious; a hunter who stays still downwind can often get within a long bowshot. Deer startle more easily and run faster. Aim for the heart, behind the front leg, and you will spare the animal suffering and yourself a long chase.

#Hides and Meat

Every animal you take should be used. Hides go to the tanner or the leatherworker. Meat goes to the cook pot or the smokehouse. Antlers and horns fetch coin from alchemists and craftsmen.

The forest gives. The hunter takes. The wise hunter takes only what she needs.

#Fishing

When the hunting is poor, the rivers are kind. Salmon leap upstream in the warm months; a patient angler at a waterfall can fill a basket by noon. Ice fishing in winter is colder and slower, but the fish under the ice are fat and slow too.

#A Hunter's Prayer

Swift feet, steady hands, clear eyes, cold wind in my face. Let my arrow fly true and my quarry fall quickly. Let me come home with meat and come home at all.
